title: Small Surface API Garden - cleanup & followups (scratch)
body:
Quick brain-dump while going through the PR / surface cleanups — messy, iterative, intended as a single-person notebook and a handoff artifact later.

Context:
- Target: shrink the public surface area of the legacy /v1/embeddings and consolidate routing into /api/embeddings v2.
- Motivation: reduce routing complexity and make caching/kv-keying consistent for Dedicated and Hosted.
- Risk profile: low-medium if we follow canary + feature-flag gating; high if Schema v1 still used by some apps.

High-level goals (what success looks like):
1) All traffic routed through /api/embeddings v2 for new keys within 2 weeks.
2) Backwards-compatible fallbacks for older client tokens for 30 days, telemetry for usage.
3) No increase in p50 latency >5ms for embedding calls during rollout.
4) Tests added: end-to-end happy path, client-fallback path, KV-cache invalidation unit test.

Open questions (to resolve in review):
- Which internal customers still depend on the original response shape? INF-2384 lists three teams but I need confirmations.
- Do we need a transitional JSON envelope header to make v2 forwards compatible with the ownership metadata?
- How will KeyManager handle old tokens? Does Dedicated require a migration script?

Quick review checklist (my running mental model while scanning diffs):
- API surface: any exported handler names or auth scopes that leak? (grep for ExportedHandler /public/).
- Schema changes: Are new fields optional with defaults? Is decoding tolerant to extra fields?
- Telemetry: added trace/span names? metric tags include model_name and route_version?
- Caching: the kv-key composition must include route_version and customer_id — the change here removes route_version in 2 places, revert unless intentional.
- Tests: unit tests exist but no integration/system tests updated — add a small harness test that runs the router locally.
- Docs: README + API spec updated? I see API.md touched but examples still show old path.

Refactor ideas (not necessarily in this PR, but obvious follow-ups):
- Extract router-matching predicate into a single file with tests; current duplication across hosted/dedicated makes future changes error-prone.
- Introduce a thin "compat shim" module that maps v1 envelope -> v2 envelope; use it only during feature-flag period. That centralizes conversions and avoids ad-hoc checks in handlers.
- Add a small telemetry shim that stamps "compat:true/false" on spans for easier post-mortem.

Small safety plan for rollout (canary + kill-switch):
1) Merge behind feature-flag default=false.
2) Deploy to canary region (us-west-canary) with 2% traffic routing through v2. Monitor errors, p95, and embed-size distribution for 24h.
3) Ramp to 25% over 6h if no regressions.
4) Enable feature flag account-by-account for Dedicated customers after verification.
5) Remove v1 after 30 days of 0 usage and a one-week notification window.

Manual checks to run before merging to main (todo list):
- [ ] Confirm INF-2384 owners replied and updated compat matrix.
- [ ] Add integration harness test: route vs realtime KV cache verification.
- [ ] Add metric: embedding_route_version (tag) + compat_flag.
- [ ] Add migration note for Dedicated in ops-runbook (who runs it? solutions-eng/ops).
- [ ] Update examples in API.md + snippets in docs site.
- [ ] Add a quick rollback playbook in PR description (commands and old tag).

Example small code snippet to centralize compat shim (pseudo):

// compat-shim.js (concept)
// input: raw request body
// output: standardized { customerId, model, inputs, meta }
function normalize(reqBody) {
  if (reqBody.v2) return { customerId: reqBody.c, model: reqBody.m, inputs: reqBody.items, meta: reqBody.meta || {} }
  // v1 mapping, keep permissive parsing
  return { customerId: reqBody.account || 'unknown', model: reqBody.model_name || 'embed-default', inputs: Array.isArray(reqBody.text) ? reqBody.text : [reqBody.text], meta: reqBody._meta || {} }
}

Metrics + alerts to add while rolling:
- Alert if embedding route error rate (for new path) > 0.5% for 10m AND increased relative to baseline.
- Dashboard: p50/p95 latency by route_version and by model_name.
- Log sample: first 50 compat=true requests daily for 7 days (for audit).

Unresolved followups (assign later):
- Asha: talk to product about deprecation notice language and customer comms.
- Liam: quick check on Dedicated KV TTL behavior; might need migration.
- Me (Noel): add 1 integration test + write canary runbook.

Quick todos for PR description before requesting review: (copyable checklist)
- [ ] Feature-flagged change with default off
- [ ] Compatibility shim included and unit-tested
- [ ] Telemetry tags added and dashboards linked
- [ ] Canary plan & rollback steps added to PR body
- [ ] Notify Slack #serving-runtime and #customer-integrations 24h before ramp

Random notes / rough timings:
- Estimated dev time to finish tests + docs: 3-5d.
- Canary window: 24-48h depending on error signal.
- Full removal of v1: schedule a calendar invite for deprecation notice 7 days before kill date.

If I get stuck: pair with Liam for Dedicated key behavior (30m pair), then Asha for comms (15m).

Bottom line: PR direction is fine, but do not remove route_version from cache key bits in caching layer. Centralize compat mapping and keep feature-flagged gating. Keep dev/test harness so we can replay recorded v1 traffic samples in CI (use recorded sample RIFLE_20240912_emsample.json).

Notes-to-self: export the recorded 1k sample of v1 requests to /tmp/emb-samples and add a small CI job that replays them into the compat-shim to catch shape regressions.

End of dump. Will tidy up into PR description once tests land.
